slides.title: Stop checking coffee's expiry date
slides.subtitle: A different date says far more. Most people skip it.

slides.myth: A later expiry date means fresher coffee.
slides.truth: That date is often set months ahead. It tells you how long the bag is considered safe to sell, not when the beans were roasted.

slides.title: Why age changes the cup
slides.body: Roasted coffee slowly loses aroma over time. Fresh beans also release CO2 for the first days, which is why many roasters let them rest before selling.
slides.highlight: Not too old, not too fresh.

slides.title: At the shelf
steps: Look for a roast date, not just an expiry date.
Pick the most recent one you can find.
Prefer small bags you will finish soon.
Grind whole beans just before brewing.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: No roast date on the bag? That is a small warning sign. Ask where it was roasted, or try another bag.

slides.title: Look for the roast date, not the expiry
slides.body: The roast date shows how old your coffee really is.
slides.cta: Send it to a coffee friend
